annotations.text:
Five specialists under one orchestrator:

WIRE — pin map, schematic, wiring checks
BOARD — PCB layout, routing, DRC
SHELL — enclosure and 3D printing
PARTS — sourcing, BOM, stock
FIRM — firmware, flashing, serial

BENCH is the lead you actually talk to. It splits the goal, runs what it can in parallel, and only interrupts you for real decisions.

Names are placeholders — swap them for whatever your team calls these.

The agents coordinate through shared files rather than chat: netlist.json, pinmap.yaml, bom.csv, the board, the case. One owner per file, everyone else reads.

That is what makes a handoff visible in the UI — and what makes SHELL genuinely blocked until BOARD ships an outline.
Screen 4 is a LATER moment than screens 1–3: BOARD has finished and handed the outline over, so the roster shows four agents done and only SHELL running. Same chrome, different state.
Accent color is still the open decision — three candidates, each with its tradeoff. Every screen wears Volt right now; the Accent chip above each artboard swaps all three live.
